## What was wrong

`v_messages` is built at the **message-part grain** (`FROM message_part`, one row per part), but `message_feedback` is keyed by `messageId` (its PK — one feedback per message). Joining on `message_part.message_id = message_feedback.message_id` stamped the same `vote`/`explanation` onto **every part** of a message. So a message with N parts surfaced its single vote N times — inflating any aggregation over feedback (e.g. `SELECT vote, COUNT(*) ... GROUP BY vote`).

## The fix

The feedback join is now restricted to each message's **first part** (minimum `order`), so the vote/explanation appears exactly once per message while all parts still show up as rows:

```135:138:apps/backend/src/db/app-db-views.ts
				.leftJoin(
					messageFeedback,
					and(eq(messagePart.messageId, messageFeedback.messageId), firstPartOfMessage),
				)
```

The `firstPartOfMessage` predicate uses an aliased self-subquery so Drizzle emits dialect-correct SQL (verified against both SQLite and Postgres):

```70:79:apps/backend/src/db/app-db-views.ts
	// Feedback is per message, but v_messages is at the part grain. Attach it only to a
	// message's first part so the vote/explanation is not repeated across every part.
	const siblingPart = alias(messagePart, 'sibling_part');
	const firstPartOfMessage = eq(
		messagePart.order,
		sql`(${qb
			.select({ minOrder: sql`min(${siblingPart.order})` })
			.from(siblingPart)
			.where(eq(siblingPart.messageId, messagePart.messageId))})`,
	);
```

I used min-`order` rather than hardcoding `order = 0` because parts are indexed before undefined ones are filtered out (`mapUIPartsToDBParts`), so `0` isn't guaranteed to exist. The exposed columns (`vote`, `explanation`) are unchanged, so the allowlist and prompt need no updates.
